intent: Two vertical shorts cut out of our own published screencast youtu.be/6LQnRd0JxGU (@instafill_ai, 3:21, 'How to flatten a PDF for free'). The end goal is a scripted ElevenLabs voice-over REPLACING the original narration, which is live, non-native and halting. Stage 1 (done) is picture only: framing, hook cards and badge settled, source audio left on as a reference track, no captions -- those get rebuilt from the voice-over's own word timings. Stage 2 is the voice-over.

inputs._source_note: 720p, which is all YouTube serves: the 1080p rendition was not processed yet (checked across the web/tv/ios/web_safari/mweb/android_vr player clients). The YouTube token cannot help -- Data API v3 has no video-download endpoint, and Studio's 'Download original' has no API surface. No master on this machine; the on-screen clock and the Instafill account say it was recorded on a teammate's. The framing is chosen so 720p is enough: the rect is 900-1280px wide at source and lands at 1080 wide, so the picture is never upscaled more than 1.2x.

burned: source rect (215, 72, 900, 535) fitted to 1080 wide on #0B0D10
image overlay '01-free-tool.json' wipe in at 0.3s for 4.2s
source rect (0, 72, 1280, 535) fitted to 1080 wide on #0B0D10
image overlay '02-whole-packet.json' wipe in at 0.3s for 4.2s

notes: Both shorts carry the SOURCE audio as a reference track and no captions. Neither is the deliverable look: stage 2 replaces the audio with a scripted voice-over via cut-clips.py --dub and rebuilds the captions from its word timings, into new files tagged -vo. These two are never overwritten.

Three things had to leave the picture and all three are gone, verified on the render: the burned-in caption card (source y 612-660) and the taskbar (y 682+) fall below the rect; the webcam PiP (x 21-183, y 498-660) sits INSIDE it, in the same band as the buttons the demo is about, so it is masked with delogo instead. YuNet found a face in 30/30 sampled source frames and 0/80 sampled frames across the two renders.

Moments were picked on the PICTURE, not the transcript -- with the sound being replaced the original speech boundaries do not bind the cut. Short 1 drops the landing hero (91-115, 23 static seconds of a page being read aloud, and its headline starts at source x=82 where this window clips it). Short 2 drops 150-168, a progress bar that goes from 1% to done without visibly moving; it opens 3s before the status chip flips to 'Ready for Review' at 167.75s, measured off the chip's hue.

Already public on the original, so left alone: the Forms list shows real user data (Eugene Smirnov, real form names) and short 2's file dialog shows the Downloads folder. scan-pii.py + track-blur.py can blur them on request.
Source has its own branded end card wiping in at ~192s; short 2 ends at 191 to stay clear of it.
